part: 12-way (2x6) 1.27mm shrouded IDC header, keyed, right-angle, through-hole
description: Key chain connector - one at each end of each key board's IDC ribbon (CBL-CHAIN), on the main board and on the key board
package: THROUGH-HOLE right-angle, 2x6, 1.27mm pitch - envelope config/body.yaml boards.chain_hdr_*
notes: Quantity is the tracked figure chain-connectors; do not restate it. STAND-IN: Samtec SHF-106-01-L-D-RA [datasheets/connectors/SAMTEC-SHF-1XX-01-X-D-XX-PRINT.pdf - full print]. THROUGH-HOLE, so the cable's pull goes into the board, not into SMT pads. PINOUT, NUMBERED AT THE MAIN-BOARD END: 1 GND, 2 SCK, 3 GND, 4 SH/LD, 5 GND, 6 SER, 7 GND, 8 QH, 9 GND, 10 3V3, 11 spare, 12 spare - a ground between every signal in the ribbon (ADR 0001 item 1). Pin 6 is the key board's own serial input and pin 8 its own serial output, on both ribbons, so both key boards are wired alike. THE SAME PART AT EVERY J-CHAIN POSITION (chain-connectors): standing on the main board's top, and on each key board hanging from its underside directly over the main board's, both mouths facing the same way along the body, in the far band beside the LED strip (mechanical/DESIGN.md). *** THE KEY BOARD'S PIN NUMBERS ARE NOT THE MAIN BOARD'S: key-board pin = 13 - main-board pin, SET BY THE CABLE (CBL-CHAIN's -RN2 option), not by the header - a keyed socket always mates its position n to header pin n. *** KEY-BOARD PINOUT: 11 SCK, 9 SH/LD, 7 SER, 5 QH, 3 3V3, 4/6/8/10/12 GND, 1 and 2 spare - signals and 3V3 in the odd row, grounds in the even row. The key boards' sheets carry that map; place the standard footprint on the bottom side - do not hand-mirror it [datasheet, key-chain-loom.md]. Pin rows sit behind the body's back face, the tails bending down behind it (config/body.yaml boards.chain_hdr_pin_back). The key board's header pin tails come up through the board toward the grounded key plate and stop short of it, with no window in the plate: mechanical/drc.echo 'J-CHAIN pin tails clear of the key plate' - seat the header flat. FITTED BY HAND WITH ITS MOUTH AT THE SILKSCREEN ARROW: the 2x6 pad grid takes it turned 180 degrees too, and backward puts the ribbon's 3V3 on a ground pin. Placed clear of the switches by mechanical/drc.echo 'chain headers on the left_hand boards clear of the switches' and its right_hand rule. OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: the part number SOURCING: none stocked at JLCPCB/LCSC on 2026-09-27 (C17202657, stock 0), so it is FITTED BY HAND with the switches (each board's fab/*-hand-assembly.csv) - order the stand-in from Samtec (samtec.com) and check the lead time at order. The one stocked right-angle 2x6 1.27 mm header at LCSC (hanxia HX JN1.27-2x6 WZ H4.9, C42372552) is NOT a drop-in: shorter body, tail rows further behind the mouth, pin 1 unmarked, fit to the FFSD unconfirmed [datasheets/connectors/HANXIA-HX-JN1.27-2x6-WZ-H4.9.pdf].

part: 12-conductor 1.27mm IDC flat ribbon cable assembly, 2x6 IDC socket each end, notch reversed on the key-board end
description: Key chain ribbon - one per key board, main board to key board, folded closed as a flat hairpin along the body
package: Assembled length - ordered by mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain cable to order (FFSD length code)'
notes: One per key board (PCB-CLUSTER): the key chain's only conductors off the main board. STAND-IN: Samtec FFSD-06-D-xx.xx-01-N-RN2, built to length, xx.xx the length code below (inches) [datasheets/connectors/SAMTEC-FFSD-XX-X-XX.XX-01-PRINT.pdf - full print]. ORDER -RN2 - NOTCH REVERSED ON THE 2ND (KEY-BOARD) CONNECTOR ONLY (print sheet 2 fig 3). The first socket's cable leaves on the side of its key and the second's on the side away from it; -RN2 reverses the second's notch, so BOTH sockets' cables leave on their key's side (sheet 1 fig 1, sheet 2 fig 3). The main board's header has its key slot facing up, so the MAIN-BOARD SOCKET'S CABLE LEAVES UPWARD; the key board's header is the same part upside down, so the KEY-BOARD SOCKET'S CABLE LEAVES DOWNWARD. The two face each other, the ribbon runs flat with no twist, either end may go on either board, and conductor n meets key-board J-CHAIN pin 13-n. A STANDARD CABLE (no -RN2) FITS AND LOOKS RIGHT: both its ends leave downward, with a half-twist, and conductor 10's 3V3 lands on key-board pin 10, a ground. A cable whose ends both leave downward is wrong. Conductor n is main-board J-CHAIN pin n. Both sockets plug in from the same side, because both headers' mouths face the same way. LENGTH: ORDER FFSD-06-D-<code>-01-N-RN2 where <code> is mechanical/drc.echo 'key-chain cable to order (FFSD length code)' - INCHES, overall, over both sockets, with the print's -0.125 in tolerance covered (print sheet 1, note 11). The free length it gives is drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon length (derived)', in mm: never type that into the part number. It lets the lid lie face down beside the body off its far edge, the body standing on its U-bolt, with both sockets plugged in (config/body.yaml routing.chain_service). CLOSED: a flat hairpin along the body, both legs between the two plugs' heights, running the same way to the fold, so it never stands across the LED strip's light (drc.echo 'key-chain ribbon closed: hairpin leg and fold radius', 'key-chain ribbon fold no tighter than its bend radius', 'key-chain ribbon hairpin clear of the lid screws'); which way each folds is routing.chain_fold. Width and thickness: routing.chain_ribbon_w and routing.chain_ribbon_t. TO TAKE THE LID OFF: lift it, lay it beside the body, unplug both sockets. METER EVERY CABLE BEFORE IT IS FIRST POWERED, spares and replacements included: conductor 10 reaches the far socket's position 3 and conductor 2 its position 11 (hardware/boards/key-board-lh/README.md, Bring-up). OPEN, DECIDED AT M4: the part number (with -RN2); boards.chain_plug_proud, measured on the first mated pair, decides whether the cable clears the shroud's mouth

description: Series damping at the chain driving end on SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER
notes: On the main board where the MCU's pins arrive, before anything else on the net. SCK and SH/LD each reach four 74HC165s: right_thumb and left_thumb on the main board, and one at the far end of each key board's ribbon, over up to the main board's length (mechanical/drc.echo 'main board (derived)'). At that length an MCU edge sees a line rather than a lump [calc, key-chain-loom.md]. Edge-rate damping at the source - NOT series termination, which ADR 0001 rejected (as R-TERM-CHAIN) for a line that drops on four registers. Same 100R as R-SPI-SER. OPEN, DECIDED AT E14: scope SCK at the left_hand register on the real main board and ribbons; fit if it rings through the 74HC165 thresholds. Three 0805s either way

description: ESD protection on the MCU pins the key chain brings to the main board's ribbon headers
notes: FIT IT (ADR 0018). Channels: SCK, SH/LD and the chain-end SER (IO38, IO7, IO33, each on the connector side of its R-CHAIN-SER); the fourth is spare. The chain's QH into the MCU (IO40) comes from right_thumb on the main board and reaches no connector. Return to GND_CHAIN, the main board's ground pour. WHY: with the lid off and a socket unplugged, a main-board J-CHAIN header exposes three MCU pins behind 100R to a hand - and the sockets are plugged in every time the lid goes back on. It cannot be added once the board is made, and it costs pennies. PLACE IT at the left_hand J-CHAIN, which carries all three channels; SCK and SH/LD reach the right_hand J-CHAIN on the same nets. PACKAGE: SP0504BAHTG is SOT23-5 with 4 CH per the banked SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table; SOT23-6 is SP0505BAHTG with 5 CH. All channels share one common pin. It and U-TVS-SPI are two packages because each clamps at its own connector, and J-UMB and the J-CHAIN are at different places on the main board

part: Ferrite bead 600R @ 100MHz or more, DCR 0.1R or less, rated 0.5A or more
description: Series isolation on the 3V3 conductor of each key board's ribbon, on the main board
notes: ONE PER RIBBON, in series between the main board's 3V3 (DEV_3V3 - the Matrix's ME6217C33M5G LDO, reaching the main board on CBL-MCU-RIBBON) and that ribbon's conductor 10 (main-board J-CHAIN pin 10). right_thumb, left_thumb and R-SER-TERM stay on DEV_3V3 directly. IT IS ISOLATION, NOT PROTECTION: it keeps a key board's register edges off the rail that is also the MCP3202's reference. SHORT-CIRCUIT PROTECTION IS THE LDO'S OWN (ADR 0018): datasheets/discrete-and-power/ME6217C33M5G.pdf p.1 'a built-in overcurrent protector' and thermal shutdown at 160C; p.4 Ishort 350mA TYPICAL at VOUT = 0V, with no min or max. The short to expect is a socket forced or a ribbon pinched across conductors 9/10 (main-board J-CHAIN pins 9/10) at reassembly: the whole 3V3 rail collapses, the Matrix does not start, and it is seen on the bench before the lid is closed. VERIFY AT E1: short one ribbon's 3V3 to GND through 1 ohm at J-CHAIN, confirm the rail limits and the Matrix restarts when it is removed. RATINGS: rated current at or above 0.5A, because the bead carries the LDO's limit (350mA typ) for as long as a short lasts [calc]. DCR 0.1R or less: at the chain's whole key-scan-current (every key closed) that is under 3mV [calc]. CHECK AT E14: the bead and the key board's C-DECOUPLE-165 (100nF) form an LC near 0.5MHz if the bead is ~1uH below its resistive band [calc, bead inductance from memory], close to the chain's clock; scope the key board's VCC while shifting and fit C-BULK-CHAIN on the key board if it rings. PART NUMBER OPEN [from memory: 0805 beads meeting all three figures are a stock family]

part: Capacitor 10uF X5R or X7R, 10V or more, DO NOT FIT by default
description: A damping reservoir on each key board's 3V3, fitted only if the rail rings
notes: ONE FOOTPRINT PER KEY BOARD, on its root sheet (C-BULK-CHAIN-LH, -RH), dnp and out of every order: the board is ordered with it empty. FB-CHAIN and C-DECOUPLE-165 form an LC near half the chain clock (FB-CHAIN row); a bulk capacitor's ESR damps it. Decided at bring-up: scope the key board's VCC while shifting (hardware/boards/key-board-lh/README.md), and fit it if the rail rings. A footprint now costs nothing; adding one after the first order is a respin

description: Pull-up on the chain-end serial input, on the main board
notes: left_hand's SER, which leaves on conductor 6 of its ribbon (main-board J-CHAIN pin 6, key-board pin 7). ON THE MAIN BOARD at that ribbon's J-CHAIN, on the connector side of R-CHAIN-SER - so the two key boards stay identical. Holds the chain-end input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware DRIVES it from IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail (3.3V x 100/10100) - so an end-to-end self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, and through both ribbons in both directions) is a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice. Fit it. Whether firmware uses it is decided at E4
